newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Ayala unit plans 3.0 bln peso land bank.
newsitem.headline: Ayala unit plans 3.0 bln peso land bank.

text.p: Laguna Properties Holdings Inc (LPHI), the mass housing arm of Philippine real estate giant Ayala Land Inc, said on Thursday it has earmarked 3.0 billion pesos to increase its land bank to 1,000 hectares by the middle of next year.
LPHI president Manuel Colayco told reporters that by the end of this year, the company hopes to have 500 hectares.
It aims to sell 3,500 units catering to low- to middle-income home-buyers in 1997 goal, 75 percent higher than its 1996 estimate of 2,000, he said. In 1995, LPHI sold 1,500 units.
"We're aiming to be a leader in the middle-range housing," said Colayco. This segment of the market covers those who can afford to buy homes costing 1.5 to 5.0 million pesos.
LPHI unveiled on Thursday the first of a new line of middle-range housing units using French technology.
Four hundred and fifty houses using this technology are being built on a 16-hectare site just south of Manila and about 90 have already been presold, LHPI officials said.
They are being sold at an average of 4.0 million pesos.
LHPI bought the "Concorde system," which involves steel frames and pre-cast panels, from Maison Individuelles SA, part of the Compagnie Generale des Eaux Group.

Colayco said LHPI would spend some 250 million pesos on setting up a factory to manufacture these housing parts. The factory would enable LHPI to build an initial 1,500 units yearly to be raised to 3,500 after three or four years.
